business_summary.text: Sumitomo Chemical India is an agrochemicals company making technical grade actives and formulations (insecticides, herbicides, fungicides, PGRs, metal phosphides, animal nutrition and public health) across five plants, selling domestically through 15,000+ distributors and exporting to ~50 countries.

call_points.text: No revenue or margin guidance given; the filing says the business is best monitored annually given seasonality.
Q1 domestic demand was hit by a delayed monsoon, 40% rainfall deficit and ~20% lower early kharif sowing.
Exports grew 26% YoY to 16% of revenue, led by South America, Asia ex-India and Africa; Japan and North America declined.
Overall optimal capacity utilisation is ~80% to 90% for technical grade actives (TGAI).
Topgrain and Helibax (Pyridalyl + Emamectin) remain on track for launch during Q2FY27.
Board reconstitution effective 1 September 2026: Dr. Suresh Ramachandran becomes Managing Director; Chetan Shah moves to Non-Executive Chairman.
The company plans to invest ~15% of consolidated EBITDA every year in manufacturing upgradation and capacity expansion.
FY27 outlook is only 'cautiously optimistic'; no revenue or margin number given
Pure agro business grew 5-6% in FY26, almost entirely volume; pricing stable
₹150 Cr Dahej capex on track, commercialisation in about 2 years; further projects of similar size planned
Essentially debt-free; cash and liquid investments ₹2,113 Cr at 31 March 2026; ROCE 31%
Animal nutrition distribution to restart; margin only 4-5%, so revenue up but profit impact limited
Custom synthesis (CRAMS) revenue roughly ₹100-150 Cr; growth expected once projects are implemented
Input costs up 10-25% by product; three price hikes taken since 15 March, fourth under review
Leadership change: Dr. Suresh Ramachandran to become MD from 1 September 2026; Chetan Shah to move to non-executive chairman
India elevated to top tier for early-stage testing of parent SCC's new molecules; two received for trials

guidance.statement: Invest ~15% of consolidated EBITDA every year for upgradation of manufacturing facilities and capacity expansion

industry: Commodities > Chemicals > Fertilizers & Agrochemicals > Pesticides & Agrochemicals

operating_notes.text: Custom synthesis (CRAMS) revenue is roughly ₹100-150 Cr a year, with growth expected once projects are implemented from next financial year.
Biologicals contribute about 8-10% of revenue versus an industry average below 5%; specialty products are 30% of domestic revenue.
Exports and imports are roughly USD 70-80 million each annually, making net currency exposure largely self-hedging.
Overall optimal capacity utilisation is ~80% to 90% for technical grade actives (TGAI).
Exports were 16% of Q1FY27 revenue, up from 13% a year ago, with growth of 26% YoY.
Top 10 products contribute less than 45% of total annual revenue and no single molecule more than ~17%.

timeline.summary: On 28 May 2026 Sumitomo Chemical India's FY26 earnings call reported record FY26 PAT of ₹543 Cr (+7%) and EBITDA margin of 20.7%, with no numeric FY27 guidance and a leadership transition announced for 1 September 2026.
